theorems.statement: theorem empty_write_has_ordered_events (byte : UInt8) : (uartWriteByte (default : State) byte).state.events = #[.fence, .write UART.rbrThrOffset byte, .fence]

theorem response_size (status : UInt8) (requestId value : UInt64) : (encodeResponse status requestId value).size = 24

branch_effect_evidence.evidence_boundary: QEMU directly observes both selected UART behavior and the scratch+64 byte read back by compiled Lean: false returns 0x5a00 after writing 0x5a, while true emits 0xa5 and returns 0x3c01 with the initialized 0x3c sentinel preserved; source/model and exclusive pre/post-LLVM CFG audits bind those observations to the selected branches

observations.selected_effect: raw UART 0xa5 emitted; scratch+64 preserved at sentinel 0x3c

gate_6.security_interpretation: compiled checked Core0 code performs declared ordered MMIO and checked ordinary-RAM access inside one trusted M-mode image; this is not isolation against arbitrary privileged machine code
limitations: Finite model/source probes and local device lemmas are not a compiler-correctness or hardware-correctness proof.
The machine result is specific to the pinned QEMU virt ns16550a model; it is not a physical-board claim.
Transmit backpressure is exercised through QEMU's stdio serial backend and is not a UART latency measurement.
Gate 6 remains polling-only and adds no trap substrate, interrupts, scheduler, or managed runtime.
This result does not complete G1 or G2.
